question: What is the primary action a nurse must confirm before beginning last offices?

options.A: Formal verification of death by a doctor
options.C: Notification of the hospital security team
options.D: Disinfection of the entire ward unit

explanation: Post-mortem care should only commence after a medical practitioner has officially pronounced and certified the death. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why is recording the exact time of death critical in clinical practice?

options.A: It is required for legal and administrative documentation
options.B: It guides the nurse on how to clean the bed
options.C: It dictates the specific mortuary fee to be paid
options.D: It determines when the family can visit the ward

explanation: The exact time of death is a vital legal data point needed for official death certificates and hospital records. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h1)

question: A Muslim patient passes away in the ward. What should the nurse prioritize regarding their cultural needs?

options.A: Swift preparation and prompt release of the body
options.B: Delaying procedures for a mandatory 24-hour waiting period
options.C: Insisting that an autopsy be performed immediately
options.D: Removing all religious symbols from the bedside

explanation: Islamic customs emphasize quick burial, making timely execution of last offices essential for the family. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h2)

question: Which type of death requires the nurse to leave all tubes intact and avoid washing the body?

options.A: A death resulting from chronic kidney disease
options.B: A death due to uncomplicated malaria
options.D: An expected death in a palliative care ward

explanation: Unnatural or suspicious deaths fall under coroner jurisdiction, requiring evidence to be preserved untouched on the body. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h2)

question: Why must a nurse wear personal protective equipment during last offices?

options.A: To comply with hospital fashion regulations
options.B: To keep the nurse's uniform from getting wrinkled
options.C: To comfort the grieving relatives visiting the room
options.D: To prevent exposure to potential body fluid transmission

explanation: Post-mortem bodies may still harbor pathogens, making barrier protection essential for nurse safety. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h3)

question: When is the best time for a nurse to gather all necessary supplies for last offices?

options.A: Before beginning any physical care on the body
options.B: Only when the mortuary attendants arrive at the ward
options.C: After washing and dressing the deceased patient
options.D: While waiting for the doctor to certify the death

explanation: Gathering supplies beforehand ensures an efficient, respectful, and uninterrupted procedure. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for placing cotton wool in the natural orifices of the deceased?

options.A: To prepare the body for immediate embalming
options.B: To prevent leakage of body fluids after death
options.C: To block air entry into the lungs post-mortem
options.D: To improve the facial appearance of the patient

explanation: Relaxation of muscles and sphincters after death can cause fluid discharge, which cotton wool packing helps control. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h4)

question: How should the body be positioned immediately after death is confirmed?

options.A: Supine with arms straight or crossed over the abdomen
options.B: In a lateral recovery position to aid drainage
options.C: Sitting upright supported by cardiac pillows
options.D: Semi-Fowler's position with knees slightly elevated

explanation: A flat, supine alignment prevents the body from stiffening in an awkward posture due to rigor mortis. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h4)

question: Who should witness the collection and logging of a deceased patient's valuables?

options.A: The hospital security guard on duty
options.B: Another nurse or hospital staff member
options.C: The mortuary attendant receiving the body
options.D: Any visitor standing in the hallway

explanation: Having a second staff member present ensures transparency and protects against accusations of theft or loss. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h5)

question: What is NOT a necessary detail to include in the official post-mortem nursing documentation?

options.A: The exact time the death was pronounced by the doctor
options.B: The personal opinions of the nurse about the family's grief
options.C: The names and signatures of staff handling patient valuables
options.D: The time the body was transferred to the hospital mortuary

explanation: Nursing documentation must remain objective, factual, and professional, omitting subjective emotional commentary. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h5)

question: Why is it important to transport the covered body discreetly through hospital corridors?

options.A: To maintain respect for the deceased and protect other patients from distress
options.B: To prevent the mortuary trolley from breaking down in public areas
options.C: To ensure the body does not get exposed to direct sunlight
options.D: To follow strict infection control rules for outdoor pathways

explanation: Discreet transfer preserves the dignity of the dead and shields vulnerable recovering patients from psychological shock. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h6)

question: What document must accompany the body during transfer to the hospital mortuary?
explanation: Clear identification tags and handover forms are necessary to prevent mix-ups and ensure legal chain of custody. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h6)
